sections.h2: Which selling route fits a Knoxville house
sections.html:
Knoxville owners choose between an agent listing, a sale without an agent, and a buyer who pays cash for the home as it stands. The right route depends on repairs, timing and what the house is worth to an ordinary buyer.

The city had an estimated 202,021 residents on July 1, 2025, a 6.0% gain on the 2020 base. Owners live in only 46.6% of Knoxville housing, and the 2020-2024 median value of those homes is $239,700. Landlords and heirs holding a second house are therefore a big share of local sellers.

  • Agent listing: the widest exposure, plus showings, repair requests after the buyer's inspection and carrying costs while you wait.
  • Sale without an agent: you keep the commission and take on the contract, the deed and closing coordination.
  • Cash purchase: no showings, a closing date you choose, and a price that reflects the repairs the buyer absorbs.

Buyers sort the city into five areas, and each pulls a different kind of house.

  • Downtown and the Old City: mixed residential and commercial blocks around Gay Street, next to the University of Tennessee campus and Fort Sanders.
  • South Knoxville: across the river, with Vestal, Island Home Park and Colonial Hills, served by Chapman Highway and Alcoa Highway.
  • West Knoxville: Sequoyah Hills, Bearden, Cedar Bluff and the Kingston Pike corridor near West Town Mall and Turkey Creek.
  • East Knoxville: Parkridge, Burlington, Morningside and Five Points along Magnolia Avenue.
  • North Knoxville: Fountain City and Inskip-Norwood, with Broadway as the commercial spine.

Interstates 40 and 75 meet west of downtown, I-640 bypasses the north side, and I-140 (Pellissippi Parkway) links West Knoxville with McGhee Tyson Airport and Maryville. The average commute for Knoxville workers is 20.2 minutes.

Ridges such as Sharp's Ridge, Brown Mountain and Beaver Ridge mean many lots slope, and First, Second and Third Creek cut through older neighborhoods. Inspectors tend to start with drainage, crawl space moisture, roof age and cooling equipment. Owners who would rather skip that work sometimes prefer an as-is buyer.

sections.h2: City and Knox County tax bills
sections.html:
A house inside the city receives two bills, one from the City of Knoxville and one from Knox County, and an unpaid balance on either follows the property to its next owner. The city is clear that a seller's promise to pay does not change what it may collect from the buyer.

Knoxville property tax rules
Tax ruleWhat applies
City bill dueOctober 1
City delinquency dateMarch 1, with penalty and interest of one percent each per month
City early-payment discount1% on real estate if paid before October 31
Residential assessment25% of appraised value
Commercial assessment40% of appraised value
Reappraisal cycleEvery two years
AppealsKnox County Board of Equalization, June hearings

The county assessor sets values and answers at 865-215-2360. The city revenue office at 865-215-2084 can produce a bill for a property when a buyer asks for one. Closing agents divide the tax year between the two parties, so request the proration sheet before you sign.

You can sell it, and the sale needs no city approval, but ask the Business Tax Office how a permit is handled when ownership changes. The city requires a permit for any stay under 30 days, and its ordinance has applied since January 2018.

  • Type 1 permits cover owner-occupied homes in residential areas.
  • Type 2 permits cover non-owner-occupied units in non-residential areas.
  • Applications and yearly renewals go through the Business Tax Office.
  • The city pays Host Compliance to match online listings against permits, and unpermitted owners can be cited.

A 24-hour complaint line (865-337-8275) is part of that program, which is another reason to settle permit status before you list.

sections.h2: Permits and records that can slow a closing
sections.html:
Open or missing building permits are the records most likely to hold up a Knoxville deal. The city runs permits through its Plans Review and Inspections portal, with separate tracks for single-family and townhouse construction, mechanical, electrical and plumbing work, and home occupations.

The Knox County Property Assessor looks at each property every other year and also checks permit progress, so a remodel or addition can change the appraised value. If you added a room, you can ask the assessor for a field review so the record matches the house. A new owner's name shows up in the assessor's system about a week after the deed is filed, and the state requires a sales questionnaire whenever title changes hands.

sections.h2: How a Knoxville deed is recorded
sections.html:
The signed deed goes to the Knox County Register of Deeds in Suite 225 of the City County Building, 400 Main Street. Staff say most documents are recorded the day they arrive, that signatures need a notary or two witnesses, and that no deadline exists for recording, though delay can cause legal trouble.

Tennessee's state transfer tax is 37 cents on every $100 of the sale price. The Register records documents but cannot draft a deed or give legal advice, and a certified copy of a lost deed costs $1.00 a page. The county also offers a free email alert when a document is recorded under your name. Call 865-215-2330 for the fee on your document.

sections.h2: Tax help for older or disabled homeowners
sections.html:
The Knox County Trustee runs two programs for people who live in the home they own, and both need a new application every year. These are the 2026 figures.

  • Elderly or disabled homeowner relief: a state-funded credit of up to $85, with a combined 2025 income limit of $38,470.
  • Owners with a total service-connected disability, and their widows or widowers: up to $444, with no income cap.
  • Senior tax freeze: open at age 65 and over with combined income below $63,470, covering a single home and up to five acres.

Relief is a payment credit and not an exemption, so the bill still arrives. Selling mid-year? Ask the Trustee how the credit is treated before closing.

Gather your city bill, county bill, a payoff letter and any permit papers, then ask the title company to confirm who is on the deed. If heirs are selling, the person with authority over the estate must be able to sign. A death can change ownership without a new deed when the right wording and a death certificate are recorded, so ask the title company or a probate attorney what your case needs.

faqs.q: Do repairs have to be done before a Knoxville sale?
faqs.a: No, repairs are your decision. An as-is purchase folds the needed work into the offer price, whereas a listing invites inspection requests.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for unpaid Knoxville property tax after a sale?
faqs.a: The new owner inherits it. Delinquent tax stays with the parcel regardless of what the contract says, so call the Revenue Office and clear old balances first.

faqs.q: How soon can a Knoxville sale close?
faqs.a: It depends mostly on title work and on whether the buyer needs a loan. Once closing is done, the Register of Deeds records documents generally the day they arrive.

faqs.q: Can heirs sell a house they inherited in Knoxville?
faqs.a: Yes, once the person with authority over the estate can sign the deed. Ask the title company or a probate attorney what your case needs.

faqs.q: What are the Knox County recording costs?
faqs.a: Tennessee statute sets the recording fee, and the state transfer tax adds 37 cents on every $100 of price. Call the Register of Deeds at 865-215-2330 for the fee on your particular document.
